correctness.rationale: The proof establishes the coatom criterion directly, computes the exact beta marginal and conditional coupon law, and derives a sharp inverse-moment boundary. The β=m+1 limit follows from mR⇒Exp(1), nonpositive covariance of missing coatom indicators, and concentration on either side of xy=1; fixed β follows from a beta small-shape tail and uniform logarithmic bounds. All normalized cases m=1..3, n=0..4 at three rational precision choices passed independent exact enumeration (15,159 weighted contexts). Infinite statements are analytically proved rather than inferred from finite enumeration.

value.rationale: This is a motivated structural completion statistic of Felde–Hanika random formal contexts. It quantifies a non-obvious phenomenon: in the standard simplex-uniform model completion happens on a polynomial scale with a Fréchet limit yet has infinite mean at every finite size; at fixed precision the same operation requires exponential time with an exponential log law. These are complete natural scaling laws, not a routine small parameter variation; the exact integrability boundary explains why conditional averages cannot measure unconditional generation costs.
